about.title: Fortuna Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Fortuna is a small city, but the products used here — from tools and vehicle parts sold along S Fortuna Boulevard and Main Street to appliances, machinery, and consumer goods found in local homes — come from the same manufacturers and supply chains found statewide. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the person hurt often has grounds for a claim even without proving anyone acted carelessly. California's strict liability rule means the focus stays on the product itself, not on excuses from a manufacturer or retailer. If you were injured near Rohnerville Road, 12th Street, or anywhere else in Fortuna by a product that didn't work the way it should have, LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who evaluates these cases every day, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Fortuna Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Works in Your Favor
items.desc: California generally doesn't require proof that a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused harm. This can simplify what you need to show to move a claim forward.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law. An attorney can help sort out which parties belong in your claim.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact and unaltered is often critical to a product liability case. An independent attorney can advise you on how to protect that evidence right away.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from many other injury claims that require proof of carelessness.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if it's safe to do so. Don't repair, discard, or alter it, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these cases.

items.question: Is this relevant if my injury happened somewhere ordinary in Fortuna, like at home?
items.answer: Yes — product liability claims aren't tied to a specific location like a roadway or intersection. Whether the injury happened in a house near Main Street or at a business along 12th Street, what matters is the product and how it failed, not where you were standing.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys, and those attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
